# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Gentle, fine, and lovely spring rain had descended throughout the entire day, appearing to subtly suggest and murmur about emerging violets and mayflowers. Pearl-gray mists had obscured the low shore fields, the gulf, and the harbour. However, as night fell, the precipitation stopped, and the ocean winds swept the mists away. Small, flaming roses of clouds were scattered across the sky above the harbour. Past this, the hills appeared dark when set against an extravagant display of crimson and daffodil. Over the bar, a large, silver evening star kept vigil. A lively, leaping wind that had just arisen blew from Fern Hollow, filled with the resinous scents of wet mosses and fir. This breeze murmured among the ancient spruces encircling the cemetery and disturbed Grace’s magnificent curls as she rested upon Hezekiah Pollock’s tombstone, her arms encircling Ida and Mary Stubbs. Facing them on a different tombstone sat Tobias and Rupert, and everyone was feeling somewhat mischievous following a whole day of being confined indoors.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0000 }

“The atmosphere simply glows this evening, doesn't it? You know, it has been cleansed so thoroughly,” Grace remarked with joy.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0001 }

Grace appeared entirely too cheerful to Mary Stubbs, given the details she was aware of, or imagined she was aware of, causing her to gaze at her with a somber expression. There was a thought resting on Mary’s mind that she intended to voice prior to returning home. Having been dispatched to the manse by Mrs. Kerr to deliver a batch of fresh eggs, she had received instructions not to remain beyond thirty minutes. As that allotted time was almost exhausted, Mary unfolded her legs from beneath her where they had grown stiff, and remarked suddenly,
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0002 }

“Forget about the air. Simply hear what I have to say. You youths from the manse simply must conduct yourselves far better than you have been doing throughout this spring—it comes down to that alone. I came up this very evening with the sole intention of informing you of this. The manner in which folks are discussing you is dreadful.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0003 }

“What have we been doing now?” exclaimed Grace with surprise, wrenching her arm from Mary’s grasp. The lips of Ida quivered as her delicate little spirit cringed inside her. Mary never failed to be so savagely blunt. A whistle came from Tobias out of defiance. He intended to show Mary that her outbursts did not affect him. Regardless, the way they acted was none of her concern. By what authority was she scolding them about their behavior?
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0004 }

“You are doing it now, just like you are doing it all the time,” Mary snapped back. “The moment people stop discussing one of your shenanigans, you commit another to get them talking once more. It appears to me that you have no concept of how the children of a manse should conduct themselves!”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0005 }

“It's possible you could inform us,” Tobias said, his tone dripping with sarcasm.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0006 }

Mary completely failed to grasp sarcasm.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0007 }

“I can inform you about the consequences if you fail to master proper behavior. Your father will be requested to resign by the session. So there, Master Tobias-know-it-all. Mrs. Hector Twiss uttered those words to Mrs. Kerr. They reached my ears. Whenever Mrs. Hector Twiss visits for tea, my ears are invariably alert. It was her statement that every one of you was deteriorating further, and even though such an outcome was anticipated given that you lacked anyone to raise you, the congregation nevertheless could not be required to tolerate it for much longer, meaning an action would need to be taken. Continuous laughter is directed at you by the Methodists, which damages feelings among the Presbyterians. According to her, a strong application of birch tonic is required by all of you. Lor’, were such a thing capable of making people righteous, a young saint is what I ought to be. My reason for sharing this with you is not a desire to wound your feelings. My sympathy goes out to you”—Mary was past mistress of the gentle art of condescension. “It is clear to me that given how things stand, your prospects are limited. Yet, the same level of allowance I make is not granted by others. According to Miss Drew, a frog was inside Rupert’s pocket during Sunday School this past Sunday, and during her recitation of the lesson, it leaped out. Her intention is to relinquish the class, so she says. What is the reason you fail to leave your insecks at home?”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0008 }

“I put it right back inside,” Rupert said. “It was just a harmless little frog! I also hope that old Odette Drew stops teaching our class. She is awful. Her very own nephew carried a filthy wad of tobacco in his pocket and invited us boys to take a chew while Elder Clow was offering a prayer. That must be far worse than a frog.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0009 }

“No, on account of frogs being more out of the blue. A bigger stir is caused by them. Furthermore, he didn't get caught doing it. On top of that, a terrible scandal was created by that praying contest you held last week. It's the talk of everyone.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0010 }

“Why, the Carrows took part in that just like we did,” Grace shouted angrily. “Bess Carrow was actually the one who proposed it to begin with. And the prize was won by Edmund.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0011 }

“Well, regardless, you are given the credit for it. Had you not done it inside the graveyard, it would not have been quite so awful.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0012 }

“A graveyard would make a particularly fine location for praying, in my opinion,” Tobias fired back.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0013 }

“When you were engaged in prayer, Deacon Hazard traveled by,” Mary remarked, “and after taking note of your hands resting across your belly and listening as you uttered a moan following each statement, he witnessed you. It appeared to him that you were mocking him.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0014 }

“Indeed I was,” announced unashamed Tobias. “Except I was unaware he was passing, naturally. It was merely a nasty coincidence. My prayers weren't truly sincere—I was aware I stood no likelihood of taking the award. Thus, I was simply deriving whatever amusement I was able to from the situation. Edmund Carrow is capable of praying fantastically. Why, his praying abilities match those of dad.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0015 }

“Ida is the sole person among US who truly enjoys prayer,” Grace remarked thoughtfully.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0016 }

“Indeed, if our prayers cause such offense to others, we have to stop doing it,” Ida lamented.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0017 }

“Well, you are allowed to pray as much as you like, just not within the cemetery—and do not turn it into a joke. It was that which caused such trouble—that, along with holding a tea-party atop the gravestones.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0018 }

“We had not.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0019 }

“Well, a soap-bubble gathering then. You possessed something. The folks from across the harbour insist you hosted a tea-party, though I am ready to believe you. And you made use of this tombstone for a table.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0020 }

“Indeed, Martha refused to allow us to blow bubbles indoors. On that day, her temper was dreadful,” Tobias clarified. “Furthermore, this ancient slab functioned as such a splendid table.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0021 }

“Were they not lovely?” exclaimed Grace, her eyes shining as she recalled the memory. “Like tiny magical realms, they showed the trees, the hills, and the harbour, and after we released them, they drifted off toward Fern Hollow.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0022 }

“Every single one except for a solitary one, which flew past and shattered against the steeple of the Methodist church,” Rupert remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0023 }

“I am happy that we accomplished it a single time, at least, prior to discovering that it was incorrect,” Grace stated.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0024 }

“Blowing them on the lawn would not have been wrong,” Mary said with impatience. “It appears I am unable to knock sense into your heads. You have been informed frequently enough that playing in the graveyard is something you shouldn't do. About it, the Methodists are sensitive.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0025 }

“We forget,” Grace remarked in a mournful tone. “And the lawn is extremely tiny—and contains so many caterpillars—and is packed with bushes and such. It is impossible for us to remain in Fern Hollow perpetually—and where else can we head?”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0026 }

“It is your actions in the cemetery that cause trouble. Just sitting in this place and speaking softly, like we are doing this very moment, would not be an issue. Though I cannot say what the outcome will be, I am certain Elder Warren intends to talk to your pa regarding the matter. Deacon Hazard happens to be his cousin.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0027 }

“I wish they would leave father alone regarding us,” Ida remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0028 }

“Indeed, folks believe that he should pay you a bit more attention. I do not—I comprehend his nature. In certain respects, he is merely a youth himself—that is his true character, and he requires somebody to take care of him just as urgently as you require it. Indeed, maybe he will possess somebody in the near future, if every rumor proves accurate.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0029 }

“In what way do you mean?” Grace inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0030 }

“Do you really not have any notion—truthfully?” asked Mary.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0031 }

“No, no. What is it that you mean?”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0032 }

“Well, upon my word, you are all so naive. Why, the entire town is discussing the matter. Your father pays visits to Clementine Ainslie. She will soon become your stepmother.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0033 }

“It isn't true,” Ida exclaimed, turning bright red.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0034 }

“Indeed, I am uncertain. My words merely reflect what people are saying. I am not presenting it as certainty. Still, it would prove beneficial. I am willing to wager a penny that Clementine Ainslie would force you to behave if she arrived here, despite her appearing so lovely and pleasant on the surface. That is how they always act until they have secured them. Nevertheless, you require somebody to discipline you. You bring shame upon your father, and my sympathies lie with him. My esteem for your father has been immense ever since he spoke to me so kindly that evening. Since that time, not one profanity has crossed my lips, nor have I uttered a falsehood. Furthermore, my desire is to behold him content and at ease, possessing his buttons and receiving proper food, alongside you youngsters being brought to order, while that old hag Martha gets relegated to her rightful position. Consider how she inspected the eggs I delivered to her this evening. ‘I hope they’re fresh,’ says she. My desire was that they were spoiled instead. However, you must ensure that she distributes one to each of you for breakfast, your father included. Cause a scene if she fails to do so. That was the purpose behind sending them up—yet Martha cannot be trusted. She is fully capable of giving them to her cat.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0035 }

Because Mary’s tongue was for the moment exhausted, a short quietness settled across the churchyard. The manse children had no desire to speak. They were mulling over the fresh and less than appetizing thoughts that Mary had put forward to them. Tobias and Rupert felt a bit shaken. Even so, what difference did it make in the end? Besides, it was improbable that any of it was true. Grace, taking everything into account, felt glad. It was only Ida who was deeply disturbed. She wished that she could go off somewhere and weep.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0036 }

“In my crown, will any stars be present?” the choir of Methodists commenced singing, starting their rehearsal inside the church of the Methodists.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0037 }

“Only three are what I want,” stated Mary, whose understanding of theology had grown significantly since she began living with Mrs. Kerr. “Only three—arranged atop my head, similar to a crown, with a large one situated in the center and a little one on either side.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0038 }

“Is there a variety of sizes when it comes to souls?” Rupert inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0039 }

“Naturally. Why, tiny infants require smaller ones than large grown men. Well, night is falling and I need to hurry back. Mrs. Kerr disapproves of my being outside past dusk. Goodness, during the time I resided with Mrs. Grimble the night was no different than daytime to me. It bothered me no more than it would a gray cat. Those times feel like a century back. Now, remember my words and endeavor to act properly, for your father's sake. I will constantly support you and stand up for you—you may be absolutely certain of that. Mrs. Kerr claims she has never encountered anyone quite like me when it comes to standing by my companions. I spoke quite impudently to Mrs. Hector Twiss regarding you and Mrs. Kerr gave me a scolding for it later. That lovely Winifred possesses a sharp tongue of her own and that's the truth. However, she was secretly delighted despite everything, because she detests old Kitty Hector and she is truly devoted to you. I can read people.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0040 }

Departing with a great deal of satisfaction, Mary voyaged away, abandoning a somewhat disheartened small party in her wake.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0041 }

“Whenever Mary Stubbs walks up to us, she consistently utters remarks that upset us,” Ida stated with bitterness.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0042 }

“I would have preferred it if we had abandoned her to go hungry in that former barn,” Tobias remarked with spite.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0043 }

“Oh, that’s wicked, Tobias,” Ida rebuked.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0044 }

“If our reputation is already so terrible, we might as well act the part,” replied Tobias without a shred of remorse. “We should just be evil if that is what everyone claims we are.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0045 }

“However, provided it doesn't cause pain to father,” Grace begged.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0046 }

Tobias shifted about in discomfort. His father was someone he idolized. Mr. Ashdown was visible sitting by his desk through the uncurtained window of the study. Reading or writing did not appear to be what he was doing. Resting his head within his hands, his entire posture conveyed an impression of exhaustion and gloom. The children were abruptly aware of this.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0047 }

“It seems likely that today someone has been bothering him regarding us,” Grace remarked. “I would prefer if we managed to get by without causing gossip. Oh—Kit Carrow! You frightened me so much!”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0048 }

Kit Carrow had crept into the burial ground and taken a seat next to the girls. Having been roaming around Fern Hollow, he had managed to discover the initial small, star-white spray of arbutus for his mother. The children from the manse became somewhat quiet following his arrival. During this spring, Kit was starting to grow apart from them a bit. Preparing for the entrance examination at Regent’s Academy, he remained behind after school alongside the older students to receive extra instruction. Furthermore, because his evenings were so packed with study, he rarely came to Fern Hollow with the rest of them anymore. It appeared he was slipping away into the world of adults.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0049 }

“What has come over everyone this evening?” he inquired. “You are no fun at all.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0050 }

“Not much,” Grace sorrowfully concurred. “You would not have much fun in you either if you were aware that you were bringing shame upon your father and causing people to gossip about you.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0051 }

“Who has been speaking of you this time?”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0052 }

“All of us—according to Mary Stubbs,” Grace said, unburdening her anxieties to an understanding Kit. “The problem is,” she finished mournfully, “there is no one to raise us. Consequently, we end up in trouble and are considered bad by everyone.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0053 }

“Why do you not elevate yourselves?” Kit proposed. “I will offer a suggestion for what you should do. Establish a Good-Conduct Club and penalize yourselves whenever you commit an action that is improper.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0054 }

“I think that is a wonderful thought,” Grace remarked, impressed by the suggestion. “However,” she continued with hesitation, “actions that appear completely innocent to US are viewed as downright terrible by everyone else. What way is there for us to know? It is impossible to constantly trouble father—especially since his presence is frequently required elsewhere.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0055 }

“If you paused to consider an action beforehand and questioned what the congregation might remark regarding it, you would usually be able to judge,” Kit said. “Your problem stems from jumping straight into matters without giving them any thought whatsoever. According to Mother, every one of you acts far too impulsively, which reflects how she once behaved. Should you deal with your infractions justly and truthfully when enforcing penalties, The Good-Conduct Club would assist you in contemplating your actions. Your chosen punishment would need to inflict genuine discomfort, as it would prove useless otherwise.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0056 }

“Lash one another?”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0057 }

“That is not quite it. Different methods of penalty would need to be devised by you so that they fit the individual. Each other would not be punished by you—yourselves would be the ones you punish. Information regarding that kind of club was something I read completely in a story-book. If you give it a try, you will observe the way it functions.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0058 }

“Let us,” Grace stated; and after Kit had left, they came to an agreement that they would. “If conditions are not proper, it is simply up to us to set them proper,” Grace remarked, with determination.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0059 }

“As Kit mentions, our actions must be honest and just,” Tobias remarked. “Because there is no one else available to accomplish this task, our group exists to improve our own standing. Having numerous regulations serves no purpose. We should establish merely a single rule, and whoever among us violates it must receive severe chastisement.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0060 }

“But how.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0061 }

“We will devise that while we proceed. Every evening, we will gather for a club meeting right here in the cemetery to discuss our actions during the daytime, and if we determine that any of us performed an act that is improper or would dishonor dad, the person who committed it, or brought it about, has to receive punishment. Such is the requirement. Everyone will jointly determine the type of penalty—it has to match the offense, as Mr. Flagg states. Furthermore, the person who is at fault will be obligated to execute it without any dodging. This is going to be enjoyable,” Tobias ended, with satisfaction.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0062 }

“The soap-bubble party was your idea,” Grace pointed out.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0063 }

“However, our club had not been established back then,” Tobias quickly added. “To-night marks the beginning of everything.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0064 }

“However, what happens if we fail to reach an accord regarding what is correct, or what penalty should be imposed? Imagine two among us favored one idea while two held a different view. An organization of this nature really should have five members.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0065 }

“Kit Carrow can be asked to act as umpire, being the squarest boy in Glen St. Agnes,” I said. “Though I suppose we are able to manage our own business for the most part, since our desire is to maintain this as confidentially as possible. Avoid uttering a single word to Mary Stubbs, for she would demand to participate and handle the raising.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0066 }

“In my opinion,” Grace stated, “dragging punishments into every day serves no purpose other than to ruin it. A punishment day should be established instead.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0067 }

“Since school won't be in the way, Saturday would be our best choice,” Ida proposed.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0068 }

“And ruin our single day off for the week,” exclaimed Grace. “Certainly not! Instead, let us choose Friday. It is fish day regardless, and fish is disliked by all of us. It makes sense to combine all the unpleasant matters into a single day. After that, we are free to proceed and enjoy ourselves on the remaining days.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0069 }

“Rubbish,” declared Tobias with authority. “That sort of plan would be entirely ineffective. We will simply impose penalties on ourselves as we progress to maintain a clean record. Everyone understands now, right? Our group is a Good-Conduct Club, formed to improve our own behavior. We consent to discipline ourselves for misdeeds, and invariably to pause prior to performing any action, regardless of what it is, to consider whether it might harm dad in any manner, while whoever avoids their duty will be expelled from the club and forbidden from ever playing with the others in Fern Hollow again. Kit Carrow will act as referee if arguments arise. Rupert, no further bringing of insects to Sunday School, and Miss Grace, kindly cease masticating gum in view of others.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0070 }

“There will be no further mocking of older people at prayer or attending the Methodist prayer service,” Grace shot back.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0071 }

“Well, attending the Methodist prayer meeting does no damage,” Tobias objected, utterly astonished.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0072 }

“Mrs. Kerr claims that is the case, stating that minister's kids ought to attend only Presbyterian events.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0073 }

“Darn it, going to the Methodist prayer meeting is something I won't give up,” Tobias exclaimed. “Ours isn't nearly as much fun as that one is.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0074 }

“A bad word was spoken by you,” Grace exclaimed. “You must discipline yourself now.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0075 }

“Only when everything is put in black and white. Our discussion is merely about the club. Its actual formation doesn't happen until it is set down in writing and endorsed by us. A constitution as well as by-laws must be created. Besides, you are aware that attending a prayer meeting is not wrong.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0076 }

“However, we are required to chastise ourselves not merely for our misdeeds, but for whatever could potentially cause harm to father.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0077 }

“No one is going to be harmed by it. You are aware that Mrs. Kerr holds crazy views regarding Methodists. Aside from her, my going causes no stir with anyone. My behavior is always proper. Query Kit or Mrs. Carrow to discover their thoughts on the matter. Whatever they decide, I will accept. Now I am leaving to fetch the paper, after which I will carry out the lantern so everyone can sign.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0078 }

A quarter of an hour afterwards, the paper was gravely endorsed upon the gravestone of Hezekiah Pollock, in the middle of which the dim manse lantern had been placed, with the children kneeling in a circle about it. Mrs. Elder Clow happened to be walking by right then, and by the following day the whole of the Glen was told that the youngsters from the manse had engaged in yet another contest of prayer, finishing it off by pursuing one another through the tombstones with a lantern. It was likely that this added detail had been inspired because, once the signing and sealing had been finished, Rupert had picked up the lantern and paced carefully over to the small depression so he could inspect his ant-hill. The remaining children had walked silently into the manse and gone to sleep.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0079 }

“Is it real, do you suppose, that Miss Ainslie will be married to father?” was the trembling query Ida had put to Grace, once they had finished saying their prayers.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0080 }

“I am not sure, yet I would enjoy it,” Grace said.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0081 }

“Oh, I wouldn’t,” Ida uttered, gasping. “She is nice as she currently is. Mary Stubbs, however, asserts that becoming stepmothers transforms individuals completely. At that point, they become terribly ill-tempered, stingy, and spiteful, and they estrange your father from you. She claims that they always do so. In not one instance has she known this to fail.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0082 }

“I doubt Miss Ainslie would ever attempt such a thing,” Grace exclaimed.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0083 }

“Mary claims that everyone would think so. Grace, she understands everything regarding stepmothers—she claims to have encountered hundreds of them—while you have not encountered a single one. Oh, the horrifying stories Mary has related to me concerning them. She claims she was aware of a stepmother who lashed her husband’s young daughters upon their naked shoulders until blood flowed, and afterwards locked them inside a freezing, unlit coal cellar for the entire night. She claims every one of them is desperate to perform actions such as those.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0084 }

“Miss Ainslie wouldn't, in my opinion. Ida, your knowledge of her isn't as deep as mine. Consider that lovely small bird she gave me as a present. My affection for it is much greater, even, than what I feel for Adam.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0085 }

“Step-parenting simply alters their nature. Mary claims it is beyond their control. Father’s hatred toward us would be far worse than the beatings.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0086 }

“You are aware that no circumstance could cause father to despise us. Stop being foolish, Ida. It is quite probable that we have no reason for concern. It is likely that if we manage our club correctly and raise ourselves in a suitable manner, father will not consider taking another wife. Should he do so, however, I am certain that Miss Ainslie will treat us wonderfully.”
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0087 }

However, Ida lacked any such assurance, and she wept until she fell asleep.
{: #nw-v05-c23-p0088 }
